answers.label: Q1
answers.solution:
Let the number be \(x\).

Correct answer = \(x \times \frac{5}{6} = \frac{5x}{6}\).

Shyam's answer = \(x \div \frac{5}{6} = \frac{6x}{5}\).

\(\frac{6x}{5} - \frac{5x}{6} = 55\).

\(\frac{36x - 25x}{30} = 55\), so \(\frac{11x}{30} = 55\).

\(x = \frac{55 \times 30}{11} = 150\).

So, the given number is 150.

answers.label: Q.2
answers.solution:
A number divisible by each of 16, 36, 45, 48 is a multiple of their LCM.

\(16 = 2^4\), \(36 = 2^2 \times 3^2\), \(45 = 3^2 \times 5\), \(48 = 2^4 \times 3\).

LCM = \(2^4 \times 3^2 \times 5 = 720\).

Largest four-digit number = 9999. \(9999 \div 720\) gives quotient 13 and remainder \(9999 - 9360 = 639\).

Required number = \(9999 - 639 = 9360\) (\(= 720 \times 13\)).

So, the highest four-digit number is 9360.

answers.solution:
Use \(\frac{M_1 D_1}{W_1} = \frac{M_2 D_2}{W_2}\).

\(\frac{12 \times 16}{10} = \frac{8 \times D_2}{20}\).

\(8 D_2 = \frac{12 \times 16 \times 20}{10} = 384\).

\(D_2 = \frac{384}{8} = 48\).

So, 8 people will paint 20 rooms in 48 days.

answers.solution:
Let the angles be \(3x, 5x, 7x, 9x\).

Sum of angles of a quadrilateral = \(360^\circ\).

\(3x + 5x + 7x + 9x = 360^\circ\), so \(24x = 360^\circ\) and \(x = 15^\circ\).

Angles: \(3 \times 15 = 45^\circ\), \(5 \times 15 = 75^\circ\), \(7 \times 15 = 105^\circ\), \(9 \times 15 = 135^\circ\).

So, the angles are \(45^\circ, 75^\circ, 105^\circ, 135^\circ\).

answers.solution:
\(\frac{25}{9} = \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^2\), so \(\left[\frac{25}{9}\right]^{-\frac{11}{2}} = \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{2 \times (-\frac{11}{2})} = \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{-11}\).

Left side = \(\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{-5} \times \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{-11} = \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{-16}\).

So \(\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{-16} = \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{8x}\).

Equating powers: \(8x = -16\), so \(x = -2\).

So, \(x = -2\).

answers.label: Q.7
answers.solution:
The number increased by 17 must be the LCM of 520 and 468.

\(520 = 2^3 \times 5 \times 13\), \(468 = 2^2 \times 3^2 \times 13\).

LCM = \(2^3 \times 3^2 \times 5 \times 13 = 4680\).

Required number = \(4680 - 17 = 4663\).

So, the smallest number is 4663.

answers.solution:
Running time = \(\frac{500}{50} = 10\) hours.

The car stops after 100, 200, 300 and 400 km. After 500 km the journey is over, so no stop is counted there. Number of stops = 4.

Stopping time = \(4 \times \frac{1}{2} = 2\) hours.

Total time = \(10 + 2 = 12\) hours.

So, the car will take 12 hours.

answers.label: Q.9
answers.solution:
Let the speeds be \(v_1\) and \(v_2\).

A train crossing a man covers its own length: lengths are \(27 v_1\) and \(17 v_2\).

Crossing each other in opposite directions, they cover the sum of the lengths at relative speed \(v_1 + v_2\):

\(\frac{27 v_1 + 17 v_2}{v_1 + v_2} = 23\).

\(27 v_1 + 17 v_2 = 23 v_1 + 23 v_2\), so \(4 v_1 = 6 v_2\).

\(\frac{v_1}{v_2} = \frac{6}{4} = \frac{3}{2}\).

So, the ratio of their speeds is 3 : 2.

answers.label: Q.10
answers.solution:
Let length, breadth and height be \(4k, 3k, 2k\).

Volume: \(4k \times 3k \times 2k = 24k^3 = 5184\).

\(k^3 = \frac{5184}{24} = 216\), so \(k = 6\).

Length = 24 cm, breadth = 18 cm, height = 12 cm.

Check: 24, 18 and 12 are all divisible by both 3 and 2, so the cuboid can be cut exactly into 3 cm cubes or 2 cm cubes.

So, the dimensions are 24 cm \(\times\) 18 cm \(\times\) 12 cm.

answers.label: Q.12
answers.solution:
The three lines are parallel. Call the vertex on the middle line V. The reflex angle at V is \(235^\circ\), so the angle between the two arms on the left (the side of the middle line) is \(360^\circ - 235^\circ = 125^\circ\).

The middle line splits this \(125^\circ\) into an upper part \(\alpha\) and a lower part \(\beta\).

Upper part: the angle 2x lies between the top line (to the left) and the arm above it. It is vertically opposite the angle between the top line (to the right) and the arm going down to V, which is alternate to \(\alpha\). So \(\alpha = 2x\).

Lower part: the angle \(3x + 5^\circ\) lies between the bottom line (to the left) and the arm going up to V. The angle between the bottom line (to the right) and that arm is alternate to \(\beta\), and the two angles on the bottom line make \(180^\circ\). So \(\beta = 180^\circ - (3x + 5^\circ) = 175^\circ - 3x\).

\(\alpha + \beta = 125^\circ\): \(2x + 175^\circ - 3x = 125^\circ\), so \(x = 50^\circ\).

Check: \(\alpha = 100^\circ\), \(\beta = 25^\circ\), total \(125^\circ\).

So, \(x = 50^\circ\).

(The figure is not drawn to scale. If the angle marked \(3x + 5^\circ\) were meant to be the alternate angle to \(\beta\) itself, the equation would be \(2x + 3x + 5^\circ = 125^\circ\), giving \(x = 24^\circ\).)

As printed there is a stray "?" after the bar; it is ignored, and the bar (vinculum) over \(9 - 5x\) is treated as a bracket.

Innermost: \(8 - (9 - 5x) = 8 - 9 + 5x = 5x - 1\).

\(3(5x - 1) = 15x - 3\).

Curly bracket: \(-17x + 15x - 3 = -2x - 3\).

\(-4(-2x - 3) = 8x + 12\).

Square bracket: \(-11x + 8x + 12 = -3x + 12\).

\(84 - 7(-3x + 12) = 84 + 21x - 84 = 21x\).

So, the expression simplifies to \(21x\).

The rectangle ABCD has its corners on the circle, so its diagonal is a diameter.

Diagonal = \(\sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{64 + 36} = \sqrt{100} = 10\) cm, so radius = 5 cm.

Area of circle = \(3.14 \times 5 \times 5 = 78.5\) cm\(^2\).

Area of rectangle = \(8 \times 6 = 48\) cm\(^2\).

Shaded area = \(78.5 - 48 = 30.5\) cm\(^2\).

So, the area of the shaded region is 30.5 cm\(^2\).

answers.label: Q.15
answers.solution:
SP of 90 pens = Rs 160 at 20% loss, so CP of 90 pens = \(\frac{160 \times 100}{80} = \) Rs 200.

CP of 1 pen = \(\frac{200}{90} = \frac{20}{9}\) rupees.

For 20% profit, SP of 1 pen = \(\frac{20}{9} \times \frac{120}{100} = \frac{8}{3}\) rupees.

Number of pens for Rs 96 = \(96 \div \frac{8}{3} = 96 \times \frac{3}{8} = 36\).

So, 36 ball pens should be sold for Rs 96.

answers.solution:
To pass a stationary man, the train covers its own length, 125 m.

Speed = \(\frac{125}{3.75} = \frac{100}{3}\) m/s.

In km/hr: \(\frac{100}{3} \times \frac{18}{5} = 120\).

So, the speed of the train is 120 km/hr.

Let the unit digit be \(y\). Then the ten's digit is \(2y\).

Sum of digits: \(2y + y = 6\), so \(y = 2\) and the ten's digit is 4.

Number = \(10 \times 4 + 2 = 42\).

So, the number is 42.

Rule: (first number)\(^2\) \(-\) second number = third number.

Row 1: \(13^2 - 4 = 169 - 4 = 165\).

Row 2: \(3^2 - 2 = 9 - 2 = 7\).

Row 3: \(?^2 - 11 = 14\), so \(?^2 = 25\) and \(? = 5\).

So, the missing number is 5.

Rule: third number = second number + square root of the first number.

Row 1: \(41 + \sqrt{4} = 41 + 2 = 43\).

Row 2: \(47 + \sqrt{36} = 47 + 6 = 53\).

Row 3: \(53 + \sqrt{9} = 53 + 3 = 56\).

So, the missing number is 56.

answers.solution:
Let the can hold \(C\) bottles.

At first it holds \(\frac{4}{5}C\) bottles. 6 are taken out and 4 poured in, a net loss of 2 bottles.

\(\frac{4}{5}C - 6 + 4 = \frac{3}{4}C\).

\(\frac{4}{5}C - \frac{3}{4}C = 2\), so \(\frac{16C - 15C}{20} = 2\) and \(\frac{C}{20} = 2\).

\(C = 40\).

So, the can holds 40 bottles of oil.

answers.solution:
Let the part lent at \(7\frac{1}{2}\%\) for 2 years be Rs \(x\). The other part is Rs \((8000 - x)\).

Interest on first part = \(\frac{x \times 7.5 \times 2}{100} = 0.15x\).

Interest on second part = \(\frac{(8000 - x) \times 8 \times 3}{100} = 0.24(8000 - x) = 1920 - 0.24x\).

Total: \(0.15x + 1920 - 0.24x = 1416\).

\(0.09x = 504\), so \(x = 5600\).

Other part = \(8000 - 5600 = 2400\).

Check: \(0.15 \times 5600 = 840\) and \(0.24 \times 2400 = 576\); \(840 + 576 = 1416\).

So, the two parts are Rs 5600 (at \(7\frac{1}{2}\%\)) and Rs 2400 (at 8%).

\(\frac{3x - 5}{1} - \frac{1 + x}{2} = 3 - \frac{x - 1}{4}\).

Multiply every term by the LCM 4:

\(4(3x - 5) - 2(1 + x) = 12 - (x - 1)\).

\(12x - 20 - 2 - 2x = 12 - x + 1\).

\(10x - 22 = 13 - x\).

\(11x = 35\), so \(x = \frac{35}{11}\).

So, \(x = \frac{35}{11} = 3\frac{2}{11}\).

(The first fraction is printed with denominator 1, which is unusual; it is taken as printed.)

answers.label: Q.24
answers.solution:
Let the length of the train be \(L\) m and its speed \(v\) m/s.

Passing the man: \(L = 18v\).

Passing the platform: \(L + 330 = 40v\).

Subtract: \(330 = 22v\), so \(v = 15\) m/s.

Speed in km/h = \(15 \times \frac{18}{5} = 54\) km/h.

Length = \(18 \times 15 = 270\) m.

So, the speed of the train is 54 km/h and its length is 270 m.

answers.label: Q.25
answers.solution:
Let Priya's age at marriage be \(m\) years. Her present age is \(m + 8\).

\(m + 8 = 1\frac{2}{7} \times m = \frac{9}{7}m\).

\(\frac{9}{7}m - m = 8\), so \(\frac{2}{7}m = 8\) and \(m = 28\).

Present age = \(28 + 8 = 36\) years.

Daughter's present age = \(\frac{1}{6} \times 36 = 6\) years.

Daughter's age 3 years ago = \(6 - 3 = 3\) years.

So, her daughter was 3 years old 3 years ago.

Total cadets = \(6 + 10 + 5 + 7 + 2 = 30\).

Central angle = \(\frac{\text{number}}{30} \times 360^\circ\).

Photography: \(\frac{6}{30} \times 360^\circ = 72^\circ\)

Aero Modeling: \(\frac{10}{30} \times 360^\circ = 120^\circ\)

Alchemist: \(\frac{5}{30} \times 360^\circ = 60^\circ\)

Art & Craft: \(\frac{7}{30} \times 360^\circ = 84^\circ\)

Music: \(\frac{2}{30} \times 360^\circ = 24^\circ\)

Construction: draw a circle of convenient radius and a starting radius. With a protractor mark off \(72^\circ\), \(120^\circ\), \(60^\circ\), \(84^\circ\) one after another; the last sector left is \(24^\circ\). Label each sector with its club and give the chart a title.

So, the pie diagram has sectors of 72°, 120°, 60°, 84° and 24°.

answers.label: Q.27
answers.solution:
1 woman's 1 day work = \(\frac{1}{16 \times 12} = \frac{1}{192}\). 1 child's 1 day work = \(\frac{1}{24 \times 18} = \frac{1}{432}\).

Using the LCM 1728: 1 woman does \(\frac{9}{1728}\) and 1 child does \(\frac{4}{1728}\) of the work per day.

17 women + 8 children per day = \(\frac{17 \times 9 + 8 \times 4}{1728} = \frac{185}{1728}\).

Work in 8 days = \(\frac{1480}{1728}\). Remaining = \(\frac{248}{1728}\).

After 3 more children join: \(17\) women + \(11\) children per day = \(\frac{153 + 44}{1728} = \frac{197}{1728}\).

Days needed = \(\frac{248}{197} \approx 1.26\) days.

So, as printed, they take \(\frac{248}{197}\) days (about 1.26 days).

(The awkward answer suggests a misprint: with 12 women instead of 17, the rate is \(\frac{140}{1728}\), 8 days do \(\frac{1120}{1728}\), the remaining \(\frac{608}{1728}\) is done at \(\frac{152}{1728}\) per day, which gives exactly 4 days.)

Let the distance on foot be \(d\) km. Distance on bicycle = \((61 - d)\) km.

Total time: \(\frac{d}{4} + \frac{61 - d}{9} = 9\).

Multiply by 36: \(9d + 4(61 - d) = 324\).

\(9d + 244 - 4d = 324\), so \(5d = 80\) and \(d = 16\).

Check: \(\frac{16}{4} + \frac{45}{9} = 4 + 5 = 9\) hours.

So, he travelled 16 km on foot.

Area of four walls = \(2(l + b) \times h = 2(12.5 + 9) \times 7 = 2 \times 21.5 \times 7 = 301\) m\(^2\).

Area of 2 doors = \(2 \times 2.5 \times 1.2 = 6\) m\(^2\).

Area of 4 windows = \(4 \times 1.5 \times 1 = 6\) m\(^2\).

Area to be painted = \(301 - 6 - 6 = 289\) m\(^2\).

Cost = \(289 \times 3.50 = 1011.50\).

So, the cost of painting the walls is Rs 1011.50.

answers.label: Q.30
answers.solution:
Let the work last \(T\) days.

A works 2 days, B works \((T - 3)\) days, C works all \(T\) days.

\(\frac{2}{10} + \frac{T - 3}{12} + \frac{T}{15} = 1\).

Multiply by 60: \(12 + 5(T - 3) + 4T = 60\).

\(12 + 5T - 15 + 4T = 60\), so \(9T = 63\) and \(T = 7\).

Check: A does \(\frac{2}{10}\), B does \(\frac{4}{12}\), C does \(\frac{7}{15}\); \(\frac{12 + 20 + 28}{60} = 1\).

So, the work lasted 7 days.
